connection_type: I have direct personal experience (as an immigrant, refugee, religious minority, or member of a marginalised group)
disclosure_text: I come from a family of immigrants. I live in a country that is full of immigrants from all parts of the world. It is a part of my identity to live in a diverse multicultural society. However, it is been controversial these past couple of years and I have seen the effect on my community.
micronarrative:
What stands out to me is that there are two sides to every story, but in reality, most things are not black and white and require a nuanced stance. I understand the importance of prioritizing local people, but I also recognize that people are fighting for their lives and are in danger, and we, in a way, have the ability to help. 

A time when I had to take a nuanced stance was during a work issue. I understood that the other person had personal problems, but the work issue still needed to be resolved. It was challenging to balance empathy and the need to address the issue at hand.

Empathy is the biggest thing. At the end of the day, we are all human. I did not code-switch in that instance; I tried to understand their perspective while still addressing the problem. In public, I act more formal, but in private, I am more expressive and friendly. I code-switch so that other people, usually white people, can understand me more clearly. It’s a way to bridge the gap and ensure everyone is on the same page.
